Subject: Dedicated capacity: peering visibility / queue observability request

Hi Mateo,

Quick ask from our infra and procurement teams as we finalize the Dedicated capacity order: we need better visibility into how tenant-level queueing behaves when EdgeNet peering (internal multi-tenant peering) is enabled. Specifically:

- Can Redwood provide per-tenant queue depth snapshots and headroom metrics for reserved GPUs?
- We want a documented behavior for short-term peering events (e.g., transient spikes that cause tail latency). Is there a way to guarantee a throughput floor during peering?
- For audit purposes, procurement is requesting a short-form addendum that specifies: observability artifacts you will provide, retention period, and a remediation SLA if queue peering causes measurable throughput degradation.

I attached a short doc with our ask (EdgeNet_SLA_ask.docx) and a small csv showing a synthetic traffic spike pattern. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign an addendum or propose alternate mitigations?

Thanks,
Sofia Tran
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
EdgeNet

Thanks for the ping — brief technical summary and proposed customer-facing language below. Long story short: we can meet EdgeNet halfway with a telemetry + operational addendum and an explicit throughput floor option, with clear caveats about enforcement and cost.

Technical summary (concise):
- Telemetry: We can produce per-tenant telemetry snapshots from the Dedicated runtime that include: current queue depth, inflight request count, 1/5/15m token/sec, KV cache hit rate, and recent 95/99/99.9th tail latency samples. Snapshots can be exported as JSON lines on demand or scheduled. Retention: configurable, default 30 days (option for 90 days for addendum).
- Throughput guarantee: We offer two flavors:
  1) Firm floor (contracted throughput floor): dedicate a minimum of X token/sec per reserved GPU (applies only to single-region reserved pools). Requires increased reservation commitment and small premium (~6% over standard Dedicated SKU). Enforcement: token-budget metering in the scheduler; we guarantee 99.5% of the floor over monthly windows.
  2) Soft isolation with burst buffer (default): soft priorities + a burst buffer that absorbs short spikes. This does not hard-guarantee throughput floor; tail latency may increase on multi-tenant peering events but we provide telemetry and automatic mitigation (traffic shaping, temporary burst reservation).
- Queue peering behavior: when peering is enabled across tenants on a shared host, peers may compete for GPU scheduler slots. Our scheduler supports per-tenant queue affinity and preemption policies; but if the customer requires hard isolation, the Firm floor (1) is the recommended path.

Proposed one-page addendum language (bullet form customers can sign):
- Observability deliverables: weekly telemetry snapshot exports (or on-demand snapshots on request), 30-day retention (option to extend to 90 days), and a per-incident telemetry bundle if remediation is triggered.
- Throughput guarantee: firm floor option (X token/sec per reserved GPU) guaranteed at 99.5% monthly availability; or soft isolation option with burst buffer and mitigation playbook.
- Remediation SLA: if measured monthly throughput for the reserved pool drops below guaranteed floor for more than 3% of measurement windows, Redwood will: (a) perform a priority mitigation within 4 hours, (b) credit 10% of monthly reserved fee for that pool for the next billing cycle, and (c) open a post-incident analysis within 5 business days.
- Limitations: guarantees apply to single-region reserved pools and do not cover customer-origin network issues or third-party peering outside Redwood control.

Attachments: I sketched a draft addendum (redwood_sla_addendum_draft.pdf) and a short telemetry export template.

Notes for sales: please surface the Firm-floor premium to procurement if they choose that route. If they prefer soft isolation, highlight: 1) lower cost, 2) visibility + mitigation playbook, 3) optional engineering-runbook for extended incidents.

Happy to jump on the call with EdgeNet if needed — I can present the telemetry artifacts and clarify enforcement semantics.

—Laura
Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

- As an alternative (lower cost) we recommend the soft isolation + burst buffer approach plus weekly telemetry snapshots and an on-demand incident telemetry bundle.

3) If you select soft isolation, we'll enable scheduled telemetry snapshots for 30 days and set up an operations-runbook call (30m) to walk through incident mitigation.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Thursday 2027-06-03 at 10:00 AM PT to finalize? If not, propose a time and we'll adjust.

On behalf of the team — Laura will be on the call to explain telemetry and enforcement details. Naomi will outline the SRE mitigation playbook.
